gen-gf-delius-unicase-gf-noto-sans-tagal: Delius Unicase writes in relaxed, bent-wire loops, all one stroke thickness. Noto Sans Tagalog does the quieter job, packing its middle zone into a dense, generous-curved line that holds up well once the text keeps going.
gen-gf-delius-unicase-gf-noto-sans-tagba: Noto Sans Tagbanwa fills most of its line height with lowercase and leaves its curves open with clear gaps. Delius Unicase brings the friendly handwriting; this one brings the tidy texture.
gen-gf-delius-unicase-gf-noto-sans-tai-l: Noto Sans Tai Le lets its ink strokes taper out before they touch, with hardly any step from capital to lowercase. And Delius Unicase answers with stout, pipe-cleaner strokes, so make the heading small and it loses its friendly bulk.
gen-gf-delius-unicase-gf-noto-sans-tai-t: Chalkboard friendliness, a bit crowded and cheerful, where Delius Unicase draws every stroke at a constant thickness, handwritten and inviting. Noto Sans Tai Tham stacks its lowercase up toward the capital line, with each c visibly open.
gen-gf-delius-unicase-gf-noto-sans-tai-v: Approachable from the first line, Delius Unicase draws a plain stripe of ink with a tall, handwritten x-height. Noto Sans Tai Viet keeps its ascenders short and pulls its terminals back from the curves, so a long stretch of it reads smoothly.
gen-gf-delius-unicase-gf-noto-sans-takri: Noto Sans Takri leaves every small round letter generously unclosed. Delius Unicase is the stencil-cut one, relaxed and handwritten, while Takri is the sans-serif that keeps its high-waisted lowercase tidy and businesslike.
gen-gf-delius-unicase-gf-noto-sans-tamil: Relaxed and loose, Delius Unicase is a skeleton outline given one fixed stroke thickness, handwritten and spaced like rungs on a rope ladder. Noto Sans Tamil looks magnified even at ordinary size, with terminals stopping far from the stem, so a long passage feels spacious and modern.
True monoline drawing gives Delius Unicase its handwritten, bent-wire look, with a pronounced x-height and no tapering anywhere. Noto Sans Tamil Supplement is stockier, so give it a bit more size.
gen-gf-delius-unicase-gf-noto-sans-tangs: Noto Sans Tangsa opens its round letters wide, on short-stemmed, tall lowercase. Delius Unicase repeats one bar thickness across the whole line, handwritten and relaxed, so a long passage in Tangsa feels welcoming and unhurried.
gen-gf-delius-unicase-gf-noto-sans-tc: Delius Unicase has no sparkle, just a constant stroke weight and a handwritten, inviting manner. Noto Sans TC runs large open counters through its tall a, e and s, and its curves open outward, so a long stretch of it reads without any crowding.
